top.title: Austin Championship: Trace Crowe grabs 54-hole lead late
top.description: Trace Crowe birdied his final two holes Saturday to get to 14 under and separate himself from three other players through 54 holes of the inaugural Austin Championship . Chad Ramey, Erik van Rooyen and Sami Valimaki all could have shared the lead heading into Sunday's final round at Fazio Canyons Golf Course if Crowe had faltered down the stretch. But the 30-year-old Crowe, who is seeking his first win on Tour this week in Texas, birdied the par-3 17th and followed it up with another circle at No. 18 as part of the final grouping on the course. "It was like 220 straight into the wind, I was just trying to hit a 4-iron as low as I could and push it just a touch," Crowe recalled. "It was actually a pretty good shot to end up in that bunker, it was a good leave. He called the lie perfect as it was just sitting uphill. "It just came out perfect and went in — me and my caddie both had a feeling I was going to make that before we got it, so it was pretty cool to see that go in," he added. Heavy winds began to impact players still on their back nines Saturday afternoon, and Crowe was no exception. After setting the course record on Thursday with an opening-round 62, Crowe bogeyed the first two holes on his back nine on Moving Day. Another square at the par-4 16th put his chances in doubt but the run of birdies at the end of his round vaulted him ahead for the solo lead. Americans Ben Kohles and Max Greyserman are two back of Crowe's lead, while eight players sit T-7 at 11 under. Ramey had the clubhouse lead for more than an hour. He got there by limiting mistakes — the 34-year-old Mississippi State alum has posted just three bogeys, one in each round. Saturday's error came at the par-3 17th, the same hole Crowe birdied from an hour later. "On a week like this to kind of finally get some good results and be in a good position going into Sunday, it's great to see," said Ramey, who entered the week No. 136 in the FedExCup Fall standings and has moved up to a projected No. 68. Valimaki, who won for the first time at the RSM Classic last November , moved into the co-leader position with a 3-under 69. He opened the inaugural tournament 68-66 after making his first PGA Tour start since July at last week's WWT Championship. "It was good to take some time off, it's actually been a long time since I felt like I could enjoy the golf course and I feel like that's the biggest key for me," said Valimaki, who battled a right wrist injury and also received stiches in his left hand. top.description: Smyth was making his second NFL appearance of the season against the Panthers [Getty Images] Kicker Charlie Smyth landed a late 55-yard field goal, but it wasn't enough to stop New Orleans Saints falling to a 20-17 defeat against Carolina Panthers on Sunday. The former Gaelic footballer, from Mayobridge in County Down, was making his second NFL appearance of the season after being elevated from the practice squad for a second successive week. The 25-year-old helped the Saints to an overtime win against Cleveland Browns last weekend with three field goals and two extra points and he was almost the hero again against the Panthers. Smyth, who also kicked two extra points, landed a 55-yard field goal with just 41 seconds left in regulation time to tie the game at 17-17. However, Panthers quarterback Bryce Young's drive set up Panthers' kicker Ryan Fitzgerald to score a 54-yard field goal on the final play to win the game.

top.title: ‘Hitting the Powerball’… Kansas City Chiefs star has never had it so good, says Ryan Clark
top.description: Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs’ newest receiving weapon showed up immediately against the Atlanta Falcons. Chiefs general manager Brett Veach provided a surprise for quarterback Patrick Mahomes at the NFL trade deadline, agreeing a trade for Josh Downs. Downs was traded away by the Indianapolis Colts to the Chiefs for a fourth and fifth round pick, a move that could end up looking like a bargain. The new Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver made an instant impact in Week 10 in his first game for his new team. Downs caught his first touchdown from Patrick Mahomes in the second quarter, catching an 18-yard pass in the endzone. NFL expert Ryan Clark reacted to Downs’ first Chiefs touchdown by reflecting on the incredible turnaround in fortunes for the receiver – after leaving the 2-7 Colts. Clark posted on social media: “Man, imagine going to sleep one week with Daniel Jones as your QB, and waking up the next with Patrick Mahomes! “That’s the football version of hitting the Powerball! I know Josh Downs feels like a new man!” Downs leaves a losing team for a winning team Josh Downs had requested a trade away from the Indianapolis Colts after their poor start to the season, and clear intention to rebuild. His Colts team were 2-7 heading into Week 10, while the Chiefs were 6-2 prior to their win over the Falcons. Downs has never played a game in the NFL Playoffs during his three seasons in Indianapolis. Now providing he can stay injury-free in Kansas City, Downs will likely finally get the chance to play in the postseason with the Chiefs. It’s hard to disagree with Ryan Clark’s assessment that he has ‘won the Powerball’ with the trade. top.title: Inside New Chiefs Acquisition Josh Downs’ Debut Vs. Falcons
top.description: Josh Downs of the Kansas City Chiefs makes a catch for a touchdown against Billy Bowman Jr. (No. 33) of the Atlanta Falcons during the second quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on Nov. 15, 2026. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs wasted no time in unwrapping their new toy. Wide receiver Josh Downs, who the Chiefs acquired from the Indianapolis Colts for 2027 fourth- and fifth-round picks on Tuesday, was involved early in Sunday’s 35-13 victory at the Atlanta Falcons. Downs, who had four catches for 51 yards and a touchdown, played in every drive of the first quarter, but it was on special teams where he first saw action. After the Falcons went three-and-out on the game’s opening series, Downs was back to return the punt, though it ended up being a touchback. He was the returner on all three of the Chiefs’ punt returns. In the second quarter, Downs really picked up steam on the offensive side. On the Chiefs’ last drive of the first half, Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker kicked a 41-yard field goal, but the Falcons jumped offside on fourth down, giving the Chiefs a first down and another offensive opportunity. It turned out to be a costly mistake for the Falcons, which would change the game. Lined up with two other wide receivers on the left side, Downs ran an option route, which is one of his specialties, and Patrick Mahomes showed faith in him despite double coverage from defensive backs Billy Bowman Jr. and C.J. Henderson. The result was an 18-yard touchdown . “That’s a trust play,” Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said. Two offensive plays before his first touchdown as a Chiefs player, Downs was targeted on consecutive plays, which resulted in a 13-yard catch and then an incompletion. Downs’ lone downside — lame pun intended — came on the Chiefs’ second punt return when he fumbled the 50-yard punt, forcing the Chiefs to start their possession on their own four-yard line. The Chiefs did have some special teams gaffes, including allowing an onside kick to be converted, but Downs was part of a prolific, downfield Chiefs passing game. Mahomes completed 22-of-35 passes for 348 yards and five touchdowns. “Pat had a huge day,” Reid said, “and was slinging it.” Backup wide receiver Andrew Armstrong scored a 43-yard touchdown on 3rd and 1. Mahomes connected with receiver Rashee Rice who had a 50-yard contested catch for the longest gain of the game. Rice and Downs have their own connection, having trained together in the offseason and coming out of college. “That’s my dog,” Downs said. The Chiefs knew they were getting a dog in Downs after seeing him lead the Colts with seven catches for 72 yards during the Colts’ overtime loss to Kansas City in Week Two. “We saw that firsthand,” Reid said. “I had to watch him live, which wasn’t good.” Further confirmation came from conversations with Chris Ballard, who the Colts fired as general manager earlier this year. top.title: Chiefs thrash Falcons as Mahomes throws five touchdowns
top.description: Patrick Mahomes was back to his imperious best, completing 22-of 35 passes with zero interceptions and one sack in a win that took the Kansas City Chiefs level with the idle Denver Broncos top of the AFC West (Todd Kirkland) Patrick Mahomes threw for five touchdowns and 348 yards as the Kansas City Chiefs thrashed the Falcons 35-13 at Atlanta on Sunday. Mahomes was back to his imperious best, completing 22-of-35 passes with zero interceptions and one sack in a win that took the Chiefs level with the idle Denver Broncos top of the AFC West. Rookie Emmett Johnson twice found the end zone, while Josh Downs had a touchdown on his Kansas City debut following a deadline day trade from Indianapolis. Cyrus Allen and Andrew Armstrong each scored their first Chiefs touchdowns, grabbing passes of 39 yards and 43 yards respectively as Mahomes dominated the Falcons defense. It was the three-time Super Bowl champion quarterback's most impressive showing since his nine-month injury absence after tearing his knee ligaments last December. "Guys made plays, you know? I gave them chances downfield, and they went out there and made plays happen," said Mahomes. Johnson -- stepping up for Kenneth Walker III, who was absent with a groin injury -- also led the Chiefs' running game, with 22 carries for 101 yards. Star tight end Travis Kelce left the field early, injuring his ankle as he was tackled taking his first catch, but returned in the second quarter. "I thought we did a great job picking up, obviously Kenneth not being here. I thought Emmett did a great job, and then the O-line gave me chances to throw the ball down the field," said Mahomes. It was another miserable day for the Falcons, who trailed 28-3 before Bijan Robinson's fourth-quarter touchdown, and have now lost three straight and five of their past six. Elsewhere, the Cleveland Browns rallied from 17-0 down to stun the Houston Texans 27-24, as Quinshon Judkins ran in a touchdown with less than a minute remaining. The Texans had led with C.J. Stroud's first-half passing touchdowns to Nico Collins and Xavier Hutchinson. The Browns fought back to take the lead with touchdowns either side of halftime, from a Deshaun Watson six-yard run, a KC Concepcion rushing touchdown and two field goals, all without reply. The Texans thought they had salvaged the win with a Stroud pass to Dalton Schultz, before Watson led yet another late game-winning drive and Judkins ran five yards for the win with 53 seconds left. top.title: Andreeva defeats Svitolina to win WTA Finals
top.description: Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva celebrates victory over Elina Svitolina in the WTA Finals in Indian Wells (MATTHEW STOCKMAN) Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva battled past Elina Svitolina in straight sets to win the season-ending WTA Finals crown on Sunday. Andreeva powered to a 7-5, 6-3 victory in a hard-fought duel in Indian Wells to complete a superb week in California. Reigning French Open champion Andreeva, 19, clinched the title without dropping a set in the tournament. She is only the third teenager after Chris Evert and Maria Sharapova to win the WTA Finals on their debut. "It feels amazing, of course I'm super-privileged to put my name in that group," said Andreeva. The teenager thanked friends, family and support staff in a victory speech, before light-heartedly thanking herself for her success. "I want to thank myself for always doing the hard work, for never quitting, for always believing in myself, for not taking the days off, for working every day, and for committing to what I have to do," said Andreeva, wearing a track-suit top with the slogan "I want to thank myself." A grueling 1hr 48min duel saw Andreeva secure a break in the opening game of the first set before holding for a 2-0 lead. Ukrainian veteran Svitolina broke back in the fourth game, conjuring a sublime angled volley to level at 2-2. Svitolina was soon back under pressure though, conceding another break to go 4-3 down before Andreeva held for a 5-3 lead. There was more drama to follow when Andreeva served for the first set at 5-4 up. She opened with back-to-back double faults to go 0-30 down, and then yanked a wild forehand wide to give Svitolina two break points at 15-40. A long forehand gave Svitolina the break to knot it at 5-5 but Andreeva hit back immediately with her third break of serve to regain the advantage at 6-5. The Russian made no mistake when serving for the set for a second time, holding comfortably to go 1-0 up. The second set followed a familiar pattern, with both players trading some brutal groundstrokes in a series of long rallies. Andreeva broke to take the lead at 1-0 but Svitolina responded in a marathon second game, breaking back after converting her seventh break point to level at 1-1. Andreeva edged back in front with a break to go 3-2 up and then held for a 4-2 lead. The next two games went with serve to leave Svitolina serving to stay in the match at 5-3 down. A fortunate net cord left Andreeva with three match points at 0-40. Svitolina saved the first and looked poised to save another, only to hit a wide open overhead smash into the net to give Andreeva the win. Svitolina, who had been thumped 6-4, 6-0 by Andreeva in the opening round-robin game of the tournament, took positives from her performance. "After the first match I was not expecting to play in the final," Svitolina said. "Unfortunately it didn't go my way but I gave it my all." rcw/amz

top.title: Cucurella and Huijsen feature as Spain surrender Nations League group lead to England
top.description: MADRID, SPAIN - NOVEMBER 15: Jude Bellingham of England gestures towards Marc Cucurella of Spain during the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Spain and England at Riyadh Air Metropolitano on November 15, 2026 in Madrid, Spain. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) | Getty Images There was a party atmosphere at a sold-out Metropolitano on Sunday night as Spain hosted England in their first game in the Spanish capital since conquering the World Cup in the summer. Luis de la Fuente’s side had won five from five in the UEFA Nations League campaign and were unbeaten in 90 minutes in 43 games, since March 2024, with this expected to see them crowned as group winners in the UEFA Nations League. Instead, England ran out the winners, taking a 3-0 lead through a Harry Kane penalty, an Ezri Konsa header and a third from Ben White. Spain did battle back to 3-2 after the Three Lions went down to 10 men after Elliot Anderson was sent off for fouling Lamine Yamal in the box, with Mikel Oyarzabal scoring the resulting penalty and Nico Williams adding another. At left-back, Marc Cucurella had a night to forget. Booked for a foul on Morgan Rogers early in the second half, he won only one of five ground duels and didn’t complete any tackles as he struggled with the threat of Rogers down England’s right flank. Going forwards, he also contributed little with only two passes into the final third and failing to find his target with his only attempted cross. In the second half, he was joined by Dean Huijsen, who came on at the break to replace Pau Cubarsí, who conceded the penalty which gave England the lead before half-time. Huijsen too found it hard going up against Kane, losing all four of his aerial duels, and also failing to complete any tackles. Where he did contribute more was in Spain’s more direct approach with Huijsen often carrying the ball forwards before launching it into the final third later on, registering six passes into the final third and a step by 92% pass accuracy overall. Spain have now finished second in the group, behind England on goal difference, which means that they will face a tougher draw in the Nations League play-off before a final four.

top.title: The full Division III football bracket, along with at least 1 major snub
top.description: The transition from a selection committee to the NCAA Power Index (NPI) has taken some of the guess work from the Division III football championship bracket. The expansion from 32 teams to 40 has ensured fewer snubs. But that doesn't mean this year's field doesn't bring surprises. Geographic limitations and the NPI's difference of opinion with the D3Football.com rankings means there's plenty to quibble about with this year's schedule. Wheaton College, the first team to beat powerhouse North Central in the regular season since 2019, went from the poll's No. 1 team to the bracket's third overall seed. Wisconsin-Whitewater, chasing its first national title since 2014, will have home field advantage all the way to the national championship game in Salem, Virginia after topping out the NPI formula. Teams with solid resumes, like Bethel and reigning national champion Wisconsin-River Falls, were left out. The New England Small College Athletic Conference (NESCAC) put three teams in the bracket even though the league didn't play a single out-of-conference game . North Central and DePauw, each ranked in the poll's top 15, will face off in a second round game that ensures at least one realistic title contender will be gone before the field is whittled down to 16 teams. top.title: England player ratings vs Spain: Harry Kane leads clinical victory to secure top spot
top.description: FBL-EUR-NATIONS-ESP-ENG - AFP England secured a dramatic 3-2 victory over Spain at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano to clinch top spot in Nations League Group A3. Goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa, and Ben White built a commanding lead that withstood a late Spanish fightback. England delivered a tactical masterclass in efficiency to overcome Spain in a five-goal thriller at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano. Despite ceding 64% of possession to Luis de la Fuente’s side, the Three Lions were devastating in transitional moments and set-piece scenarios. Kane’s clinical penalty just before the interval set the tone, before a rapid-fire double early in the second half stunned the hosts and ended their long unbeaten run. The defensive resolve of Thomas Tuchel’s side was tested severely in the closing stages as Spain mounted a spirited comeback through Mikel Oyarzabal and Nico Williams. However, England’s ability to convert three of their five shots on target proved the difference. This result ensures England leapfrog Spain to finish first in Group 3, showcasing a pragmatic edge that bodes well for the upcoming tournament cycles under Tuchel’s stewardship. Goalkeeper & Defence James Trafford - 7/10 The young goalkeeper was kept busy throughout, making five saves to keep Spain at bay for large periods. While he could do little about the precision of the two late goals, his handling and command of the box under heavy pressure provided a solid foundation for the victory. top.title: Mirra Andreeva issues strong message after winning the WTA Finals, ‘she is not getting the win’
top.description: Mirra Andreeva is your 2026 WTA Finals champion. The Russian youngster maintained her flawless status at the end-of-year event, beating Elina Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 in Sunday’s final. It was another superb performance by the young Russian, who has also defeated Aryna Sabalenka, Diana Shnaider and Jessica Pegula in the past week. Andreeva was particularly effective off the return, winning 52 per cent of all points off Svitolina’s first serve, as reported by Sofascore . Following Sunday’s contest, Andreeva was a picture of defiance. Mirra Andreeva reveals her embattled thought process after beating Elina Svitolina “It was the second time in my life where I just thought I am going to die on the court but she is not getting the win,” Andreeva told Sky Sports in the immediate aftermath of Sunday’s blockbuster. “I felt like if she wins today it is going to be over my dead body. I am going to have blisters, cramps, everything you can possibly have but I will not lose this match. “This spirit and fighting mindset helped me get through and get more brave and aggressive in important moments,” the 19-year-old concluded. Andreeva then commented on the intensity inside the Indian Wells Centre Court, before expressing her delight at claiming her first WTA Finals crown. “I felt in the first match we played against each other that she was lacking a bit of freedom but here I knew that the match would be tough. If she gained momentum she would play better,” Andreeva, who defeated Svitolina in the group stage, noted. “I felt like two of the longest games we had on her serve and my serve she won them. So we give her credit, as it was not like I was the only one winning the long points. Mirra Andreeva’s path to winning the 2026 WTA Finals Round robin: defeated Elina Svitolina 6-4, 6-0 Round robin: defeated Aryna Sabalenka 6-4, 6-0 Round robin: defeated Diana Shnaider 6-2, 6-1 Semi-finals: defeated Jessica Pegula 6-3, 6-4 Final: defeated Elina Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 “But I just tried to make her life super complicated and I was hoping that she would know even if she wins this long point or game she would have to work twice as hard to win the next one.” “This is a dream,” she added. “I had a little break down in my practice just before heading to Indian Wells as it would be the first time that I have played in singles. “I did not want to lose the match in the group and I did not lose a match at all. It is crazy, something unbelievable. I am going to celebrate, get a car!” Mirra Andreeva emulates Ashleigh Barty As per statisticians OptaAce, Andreeva has become the first player to win the WTA Finals in her maiden appearance at the event since Ashleigh Barty in 2019. Barty, a three-time major champion, ironically also defeated Elina Svitolina in the 2019 final. The Australian also beat Petra Kvitova, Belinda Bencic and Karolina Pliskova in Shenzhen, China. top.description: England hold out, for a raucous win that will rightly be held up. Sure, it might not have been what it could have been as Ben White surged in for a sensational third in Madrid… but that last word remains key. England beat the world and European champions 3-2 in their own capital, to end the longest unbeaten run in international history, that stretched back to March 2024. Spain couldn’t make it 44 games, as England just about made it to 94 minutes. That was ultimately down to a brilliant double save from James Trafford, who was one of many positives on another Nations League night of enjoyably entertaining drama. Might Jordan Pickford ’s first place have gone with Spain’s unbeaten run? Trafford had to show his best. This was never going to be easy, no matter how Thomas Tuchel ’s side made it look for 63 minutes - until Elliott Anderson’s red card. That will be the manager’s main takeaway from the game, the “proof of concept” as he put it the night before. With 11 against 11, England were denying this Spanish team the ball and creating some swift chances that the world champions were struggling to live with. That was what the game-opening goal came from. Even if there was also debate about Anderson’s follow-through in that instance, England had opened another gap in the Spanish structure while looking so more cohesive and coruscating themselves. This is a team that can sustain attacking waves much better than the one who mostly forced their way through the summer on individual impact. White’s supreme goal, that had the world champions looking at each other and pointing fingers, was the grand exhibition of that. In between, Esri Konsa scored the plundered set-piece header that his recent performances have deserved. Jude Bellingham was at that point bossing the Spanish midfield, in the kind of way people have long imagined as his career has only escalated. This, and the very confidence from such a marker of a win, are what England have to take through to finally win that trophy at Euro 2028 . nigeria.description: England snapped world champions Spain’s unbeaten run with a 3-2 victory in Madrid on Sunday to clinch the top spot in Nations League group A3. Goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White inflicted La Roja’s first loss in a competitive game since March 2023, after 44 without defeat. England’s Elliot Anderson was sent off in the second half as Spain fought back from three goals down with strikes from Mikel Oyarzabal and Nico Williams, but Luis de la Fuente’s World Cup winners could not find the equaliser. Both sides were already sure to progress, but as group winners England will be seeded for the quarter-finals in March. England coach Thomas Tuchel selected James Trafford in goal over Jordan Pickford and also brought White and Konsa into the side. Teenage star Lamine Yamal was fit to start for Spain at Atletico Madrid’s Metropolitano stadium after missing their midweek win over the Czech Republic. However the youngster did not see much of the ball in the first half as England came out strongly. Spain’s midfielder #09 Fermin Lopez challenges England’s goalkeeper #13 James Trafford during the UEFA Nations League – League A day 6 group 3 – football match between Spain and England at Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid on November 15, 2026. (Photo by Thomas COEX / AFP) Spain goalkeeper Unai Simon produced a strong reaction save to deny Jude Bellingham, while Anthony Gordon had a dangerous shot blocked. Ballon d’Or winner Kane, who beat Yamal to the award, sent an effort narrowly wide. Barcelona defender Pau Cubarsi handed England the advantage when he clumsily felled Kane in the area on the stroke of half time. The Bayern Munich hitman powered a perfect penalty past Simon, who dived the right way but to no avail. De la Fuente tried to react at half-time with a triple change, including throwing on Barcelona duo Fermin Lopez and Pedri, but England quickly found more joy. England’s midfielder #17 Morgan Rogers fights for the ball with Spain’s forward #17 Nico Williams during the UEFA Nations League – League A day 6 group 3 – football match between Spain and England at Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid on November 15, 2026. (Photo by Javier SORIANO / AFP) Konsa headed home the second from Declan Rice’s corner in the 53rd minute after the Arsenal defender was left unmarked by Spain’s defence. Four minutes later England sliced open Spain’s defence with Kane and Bellingham combining to set up White for the third. La Roja clawed their way back into the game when Elliot Anderson fouled Yamal in the area as the Spain striker ran in on goal. The Manchester City midfielder was dismissed and Mikel Oyarzabal slotted home the penalty. Spain found a second when Gordon gave the ball away and Yamal fed Nico Williams, whose shot hit the post and bounced in. Williams curled over and Trafford denied Yamal and Marc Cucurella as Spain looked fruitlessly for the goal they needed to preserve their unbeaten record. nigeria.title: Igbokoda Crash: NAF recovers black box, holds memorial November 26
nigeria.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has confirmed the recovery of the Cockpit Voice Recorder (CVR) from the site of the October 5 aircraft crash at Igbokoda, Ondo State, announcing plans to hold a memorial service and wreath-laying ceremony for the victims on November 26. The ceremony will take place at the National Military Cemetery, Abuja, in honour of the personnel and other victims who lost their lives in the NAF 931 aircraft accident. NAF Director of Public Relations and Information, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday, saying the event would provide an opportunity for bereaved families, colleagues, friends and members of the Air Force community to pay their last respects. He said the ceremony would also serve as a formal expression of the Service’s respect and remembrance for those who died in the incident. On the recovery of the aircraft’s black box, Ejodame said the CVR, alongside other aircraft fragments and relevant evidence, had been retrieved from the crash site. He explained that data recovered from the voice recorder was being analysed and was expected to contribute significantly to the ongoing investigation into the circumstances surrounding the accident. According to him, the investigation is progressing in collaboration with the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) and the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA). The Air Force reiterated its commitment to ensuring that the investigation was conducted in accordance with the highest standards of professionalism, transparency, accountability and responsibility, while supporting the independent technical processes required to establish the cause of the crash. Ejodame further disclosed that recovery operations had yielded several human remains and aircraft fragments, while the identification process for the recovered remains was ongoing. He said the operation had been particularly challenging because of the swampy nature of the terrain and the depth to which some of the aircraft wreckage had penetrated the ground. The NAF spokesman added that the Service was engaging relevant agencies to address environmental concerns arising from the recovery exercise and ensure appropriate remediation after its completion. He said the Air Force recognised the grief of the bereaved families and remained committed to providing them with sustained support throughout the difficult period. The Service also appreciated the cooperation of relevant agencies, host communities and other stakeholders who had continued to support the recovery and investigation efforts. The NAF assured the public of its commitment to a thorough investigation, responsible environmental management and the dignified remembrance of all those who lost their lives. nigeria.title: Sanusi, Ladoja warn against politicising traditional institutions
nigeria.description: By Adeola Badru The Emir of Kano, Muhammadu Sanusi II, and the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, have called for national healing, peaceful coexistence and stronger bonds among Nigeria’s diverse ethnic and religious groups, warning against the politicisation of traditional institutions. The two traditional rulers spoke on Sunday in Ibadan when Sanusi paid a courtesy visit to Ladoja at his palace in Oke-Aremo, where they stressed the need for traditional institutions to remain above partisan interests and serve as instruments of reconciliation, mutual understanding and national unity. Sanusi, who was in Ibadan to honour an invitation from the League of Imams and Alfas in South-West Nigeria, said his visit reflected his belief in a country where ethnic, religious and political differences would not determine relationships among citizens. He described the engagement as one of the positive developments needed to bridge Nigeria’s regional and cultural divides, stressing that national unity, progress and prosperity could only be achieved when people from different backgrounds deliberately reached out to one another. The Emir said although other engagements had emerged, he considered it important to honour his earlier commitment to attend the conference, even if his participation would be brief. “We fixed this date a long time ago, and even though other events came, we considered it important to honour our promise to appear at the conference, even if it is for a brief period, because they have been expecting me to come. “This invitation is part of the positive developments we have been yearning for to build a bridge where Nigerians from different parts of the country reach out to each other and come together in the interest of the unity, the progress and the prosperity of our dear nation,” he said. Sanusi also apologised for the delay in visiting Ladoja following his appointment and coronation, explaining that certain circumstances had prevented him from attending earlier. He congratulated Ladoja on his ascension to the throne of his forebears and prayed for divine protection, a long and peaceful reign, as well as prosperity for Ibadanland and Nigeria. The move broke below Friday’s low of about $67,555 and marked the weakest level since mid-August, as weekend trading extended a selloff that has followed a stronger dollar and a fully priced December Federal Reserve rate hike. It slipped toward $71,000 by Thursday evening, then crashed to about $67,555 around midnight Eastern on Friday, its lowest level since August, before recovering toward $69,800 in the morning. entertainment.title: Professor Patricia Mamko Lar Makes History as First Female Vice-Chancellor of UNIJOS
entertainment.description: Professor Patricia Mamko Lar, appointed as the 11th substantive Vice-Chancellor and first female Vice-Chancellor of the University of Jos. The University of Jos (UNIJOS) has officially appointed Professor Patricia Mamko Lar as its 11th substantive Vice-Chancellor, making her the first woman to occupy the position since the institution was established in 1971. Announced on Thursday, 12 November 2026 by the university’s Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of Council, Senator Grace Folashade Bent , during a special meeting of the 15th Governing Council, the historic appointment sees Professor Lar succeed Professor Tanko Ishaya as she takes the helm of the Plateau State institution. Born in Langtang, Plateau State, Professor Lar is a distinguished Professor of Medical Microbiology whose career has been deeply woven into the fabric of UNIJOS for nearly four decades. After earning her Bachelor of Science degree in Microbiology from Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria in 1986, she joined the University of Jos in 1987 as a Graduate Assistant in the Department of Medical Microbiology. She later went on to earn her Master’s degree in Medical Microbiology in 1989 and her PhD in Medical Parasitology in 1998 from the University of Lagos, followed by postdoctoral training at the Institute of Human Virology, University of Maryland in the United States under the NIH-Fogarty Fellowship Programme. Rising steadily through the academic ranks, she became an Associate Professor in 2012 before attaining full professorship in October 2015. Over the years, she has built an impressive body of work with more than 40 scholarly publications focusing on infectious diseases, including HIV/AIDS, malaria, antimicrobial resistance, and phytomedicine. Beyond the lecture hall and laboratory, Professor Lar has also served in key administrative roles at UNIJOS—including Head of the Department of Microbiology and Director of Linkages and Collaborations—and previously served a six-month tenure as Acting Vice-Chancellor of Yakubu Gowon University (formerly the University of Abuja) following her appointment by President Bola Tinubu in February 2025. Alongside her academic and leadership credentials, Professor Lar is a recognised advocate for women’s empowerment, having received the He4She Certificate of Award for Women Empowerment Activism in 2019. As she begins her five-year single term as UNIJOS’s first female substantive Vice-Chancellor after 55 years, she brings nearly four decades of institutional experience to the university’s top seat. entertainment.title: Ramla Ali Wins IBF and WBO Titles to Become Somalia’s First Boxing World Champion
entertainment.description: Unified world champion Ramla Ali poses in the ring with her WBO and IBF super-bantamweight belts and her coaching team in Arlington, Texas. Photo Credit: Yahya Ali/Instagram British-Somali boxer and fashion model Ramla Ali is officially a unified world champion! On 8 November 2026 at the College Park Center in Arlington, Texas, the 37-year-old athlete captured the vacant IBF and WBO super-bantamweight world titles after securing a split-decision victory over American contender Mikiah Kreps . During the ten-round bout, Ali dropped Kreps with a sharp right hand in the third round—the sole knockdown of the night—before two judges scored the contest 97–92 and 96–93 in her favour, against one scorecard of 98–91 for Kreps. With this triumph, Ali became Somalia’s first-ever professional boxing world champion and a unified titleholder in one unforgettable night. Born in Mogadishu, Somalia, she fled the civil war as a child with her family and grew up in East London, initially taking up boxing in secret as a teenager before turning it into a life-changing calling. Ramla Ali makes her ring walk behind the Somali and British flags ahead of her super-bantamweight world title fight in Arlington, Texas. Photo Credit: Yahya Ali/Instagram Her remarkable journey from refugee to Olympic athlete and champion is also the subject of the biographical feature film In the Shadows. Directed by Anthony Wonke , the film premiered at the 70th BFI London Film Festival on 9 October 2026 before opening in UK and Irish cinemas on 30 October—just over a week before she lifted her world title belts in Texas. BAFTA-winning Top Boy actress Jasmine Jobson stars as Ali alongside Peaky Blinders actor Finn Cole as her husband and former coach, Richard Moore , with both Ali and Moore serving as executive producers on the project. This championship milestone builds on a string of barrier-breaking firsts across sports, cinema, and fashion. Long before her title win in Arlington, Ali made history as the first Muslim woman to win an English amateur boxing title, the first boxer to win an international gold medal while representing Somalia, and the first boxer to represent Somalia on the Olympic stage when she competed in the women’s featherweight division at the Tokyo 2020 Summer Olympics. Ramla Ali celebrates in the ring as the referee raises her hand following her split-decision victory over Mikiah Kreps on 8 November 2026. Photo Credit: Yahya Ali/Instagram Away from the ring, she has carved out an equally notable space in global luxury fashion. Ali has graced the covers of British Vogue, Elle UK, Harper’s Bazaar Arabia, and Grazia UK, served as a brand ambassador for Cartier and Dior, and made history as the first boxer to wear custom ring attire created by major fashion houses—including bespoke fight kits designed by Dior, Off-White, Versace, Alexander McQueen, and Burberry featuring the panther emblem from Somalia’s coat of arms. entertainment.title: Uwaezu Kanu: Why Motherhood Feels Different for Women in Their 40s Today
entertainment.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. But this experience is not unique to me. Statistics show that most women globally will have their first child at 30 or 31, and we are seeing a lot more women becoming first-time moms at 35 and above. sports.description: Trace Crowe birdied his final two holes Saturday to get to 14 under and separate himself from three other players through 54 holes of the inaugural Austin Championship . Chad Ramey, Erik van Rooyen and Sami Valimaki all could have shared the lead heading into Sunday's final round at Fazio Canyons Golf Course if Crowe had faltered down the stretch. But the 30-year-old Crowe, who is seeking his first win on Tour this week in Texas, birdied the par-3 17th and followed it up with another circle at No. 18 as part of the final grouping on the course. "It was like 220 straight into the wind, I was just trying to hit a 4-iron as low as I could and push it just a touch," Crowe recalled. sports.title: Andreeva defeats Svitolina to win WTA Finals
sports.description: Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva celebrates victory over Elina Svitolina in the WTA Finals in Indian Wells (MATTHEW STOCKMAN) Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva battled past Elina Svitolina in straight sets to win the season-ending WTA Finals crown on Sunday. Andreeva powered to a 7-5, 6-3 victory in a hard-fought duel in Indian Wells to complete a superb week in California. Reigning French Open champion Andreeva, 19, clinched the title without dropping a set in the tournament. She is only the third teenager after Chris Evert and Maria Sharapova to win the WTA Finals on their debut. "It feels amazing, of course I'm super-privileged to put my name in that group," said Andreeva. The teenager thanked friends, family and support staff in a victory speech, before light-heartedly thanking herself for her success. "I want to thank myself for always doing the hard work, for never quitting, for always believing in myself, for not taking the days off, for working every day, and for committing to what I have to do," said Andreeva, wearing a track-suit top with the slogan "I want to thank myself." A grueling 1hr 48min duel saw Andreeva secure a break in the opening game of the first set before holding for a 2-0 lead. Ukrainian veteran Svitolina broke back in the fourth game, conjuring a sublime angled volley to level at 2-2. Svitolina was soon back under pressure though, conceding another break to go 4-3 down before Andreeva held for a 5-3 lead. There was more drama to follow when Andreeva served for the first set at 5-4 up. She opened with back-to-back double faults to go 0-30 down, and then yanked a wild forehand wide to give Svitolina two break points at 15-40. A long forehand gave Svitolina the break to knot it at 5-5 but Andreeva hit back immediately with her third break of serve to regain the advantage at 6-5. The Russian made no mistake when serving for the set for a second time, holding comfortably to go 1-0 up. The second set followed a familiar pattern, with both players trading some brutal groundstrokes in a series of long rallies. Andreeva broke to take the lead at 1-0 but Svitolina responded in a marathon second game, breaking back after converting her seventh break point to level at 1-1. Andreeva edged back in front with a break to go 3-2 up and then held for a 4-2 lead. The next two games went with serve to leave Svitolina serving to stay in the match at 5-3 down. A fortunate net cord left Andreeva with three match points at 0-40. Svitolina saved the first and looked poised to save another, only to hit a wide open overhead smash into the net to give Andreeva the win. Svitolina, who had been thumped 6-4, 6-0 by Andreeva in the opening round-robin game of the tournament, took positives from her performance. "After the first match I was not expecting to play in the final," Svitolina said. "Unfortunately it didn't go my way but I gave it my all." rcw/amz

(Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) | Getty Images There was a party atmosphere at a sold-out Metropolitano on Sunday night as Spain hosted England in their first game in the Spanish capital since conquering the World Cup in the summer. Luis de la Fuente’s side had won five from five in the UEFA Nations League campaign and were unbeaten in 90 minutes in 43 games, since March 2024, with this expected to see them crowned as group winners in the UEFA Nations League. Instead, England ran out the winners, taking a 3-0 lead through a Harry Kane penalty, an Ezri Konsa header and a third from Ben White. Spain did battle back to 3-2 after the Three Lions went down to 10 men after Elliot Anderson was sent off for fouling Lamine Yamal in the box, with Mikel Oyarzabal scoring the resulting penalty and Nico Williams adding another. At left-back, Marc Cucurella had a night to forget. Booked for a foul on Morgan Rogers early in the second half, he won only one of five ground duels and didn’t complete any tackles as he struggled with the threat of Rogers down England’s right flank. Going forwards, he also contributed little with only two passes into the final third and failing to find his target with his only attempted cross. In the second half, he was joined by Dean Huijsen, who came on at the break to replace Pau Cubarsí, who conceded the penalty which gave England the lead before half-time. Huijsen too found it hard going up against Kane, losing all four of his aerial duels, and also failing to complete any tackles. Where he did contribute more was in Spain’s more direct approach with Huijsen often carrying the ball forwards before launching it into the final third later on, registering six passes into the final third and a step by 92% pass accuracy overall. Spain have now finished second in the group, behind England on goal difference, which means that they will face a tougher draw in the Nations League play-off before a final four.

sports.title: The full Division III football bracket, along with at least 1 major snub
sports.description: The transition from a selection committee to the NCAA Power Index (NPI) has taken some of the guess work from the Division III football championship bracket. The expansion from 32 teams to 40 has ensured fewer snubs. But that doesn't mean this year's field doesn't bring surprises. Geographic limitations and the NPI's difference of opinion with the D3Football.com rankings means there's plenty to quibble about with this year's schedule. Wheaton College, the first team to beat powerhouse North Central in the regular season since 2019, went from the poll's No. 1 team to the bracket's third overall seed. Wisconsin-Whitewater, chasing its first national title since 2014, will have home field advantage all the way to the national championship game in Salem, Virginia after topping out the NPI formula. Teams with solid resumes, like Bethel and reigning national champion Wisconsin-River Falls, were left out. The New England Small College Athletic Conference (NESCAC) put three teams in the bracket even though the league didn't play a single out-of-conference game . North Central and DePauw, each ranked in the poll's top 15, will face off in a second round game that ensures at least one realistic title contender will be gone before the field is whittled down to 16 teams. You can find the full bracket here . Or expand the image below. The tournament begins November 21. The national title will be decided, on January 3, on ESPN. sports.description: FBL-EUR-NATIONS-ESP-ENG - AFP England secured a dramatic 3-2 victory over Spain at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano to clinch top spot in Nations League Group A3. Goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa, and Ben White built a commanding lead that withstood a late Spanish fightback. England delivered a tactical masterclass in efficiency to overcome Spain in a five-goal thriller at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano. Despite ceding 64% of possession to Luis de la Fuente’s side, the Three Lions were devastating in transitional moments and set-piece scenarios. Kane’s clinical penalty just before the interval set the tone, before a rapid-fire double early in the second half stunned the hosts and ended their long unbeaten run. The defensive resolve of Thomas Tuchel’s side was tested severely in the closing stages as Spain mounted a spirited comeback through Mikel Oyarzabal and Nico Williams. However, England’s ability to convert three of their five shots on target proved the difference. This result ensures England leapfrog Spain to finish first in Group 3, showcasing a pragmatic edge that bodes well for the upcoming tournament cycles under Tuchel’s stewardship. sports.title: Mirra Andreeva issues strong message after winning the WTA Finals, ‘she is not getting the win’
sports.description: Mirra Andreeva is your 2026 WTA Finals champion. The Russian youngster maintained her flawless status at the end-of-year event, beating Elina Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 in Sunday’s final. It was another superb performance by the young Russian, who has also defeated Aryna Sabalenka, Diana Shnaider and Jessica Pegula in the past week. Andreeva was particularly effective off the return, winning 52 per cent of all points off Svitolina’s first serve, as reported by Sofascore . Following Sunday’s contest, Andreeva was a picture of defiance. Mirra Andreeva reveals her embattled thought process after beating Elina Svitolina “It was the second time in my life where I just thought I am going to die on the court but she is not getting the win,” Andreeva told Sky Sports in the immediate aftermath of Sunday’s blockbuster. “I felt like if she wins today it is going to be over my dead body. I am going to have blisters, cramps, everything you can possibly have but I will not lose this match. “This spirit and fighting mindset helped me get through and get more brave and aggressive in important moments,” the 19-year-old concluded. Andreeva then commented on the intensity inside the Indian Wells Centre Court, before expressing her delight at claiming her first WTA Finals crown. “I felt in the first match we played against each other that she was lacking a bit of freedom but here I knew that the match would be tough. If she gained momentum she would play better,” Andreeva, who defeated Svitolina in the group stage, noted. “I felt like two of the longest games we had on her serve and my serve she won them. So we give her credit, as it was not like I was the only one winning the long points. sports.title: How England found a new edge to beat Spain and exorcise agony of Argentina defeat
sports.description: England hold out, for a raucous win that will rightly be held up. Sure, it might not have been what it could have been as Ben White surged in for a sensational third in Madrid… but that last word remains key. England beat the world and European champions 3-2 in their own capital, to end the longest unbeaten run in international history, that stretched back to March 2024. Spain couldn’t make it 44 games, as England just about made it to 94 minutes. That was ultimately down to a brilliant double save from James Trafford, who was one of many positives on another Nations League night of enjoyably entertaining drama. Might Jordan Pickford ’s first place have gone with Spain’s unbeaten run? Trafford had to show his best. This was never going to be easy, no matter how Thomas Tuchel ’s side made it look for 63 minutes - until Elliott Anderson’s red card. That will be the manager’s main takeaway from the game, the “proof of concept” as he put it the night before. With 11 against 11, England were denying this Spanish team the ball and creating some swift chances that the world champions were struggling to live with. That was what the game-opening goal came from. Even if there was also debate about Anderson’s follow-through in that instance, England had opened another gap in the Spanish structure while looking so more cohesive and coruscating themselves. This is a team that can sustain attacking waves much better than the one who mostly forced their way through the summer on individual impact. White’s supreme goal, that had the world champions looking at each other and pointing fingers, was the grand exhibition of that. England celebrate a famous victory (Adam Davy/PA) (PA Wire) Just as crucially, it was so different to what Spain do. It was something of England's own. In between, Esri Konsa scored the plundered set-piece header that his recent performances have deserved. Jude Bellingham was at that point bossing the Spanish midfield, in the kind of way people have long imagined as his career has only escalated. This, and the very confidence from such a marker of a win, are what England have to take through to finally win that trophy at Euro 2028 . sports.title: When Arsenal Witnessed Dixie Dean Make Football History
sports.description: When Arsenal Witnessed Dixie Dean Make Football History As many may or may not know, Highbury was a theatre when it came to all matters of sport, not only football, throughout its 93-year history (1913–2006). The grand old stage hosted football, cricket and boxing, but in terms of the beautiful game, it witnessed some of the most defining moments in footballing history. However, one of the greatest individual achievements involving Arsenal actually occurred away from the Gunners’ famous home, on the final day of the 1927/28 season, almost 100 years ago. Highbury would go on to become known as the “Home of Football” . The season proved to be nothing special for Arsenal, who were yet to embark on their “Golden Era” during the 1930s, when they lifted five league titles and two FA Cups. They finished far off from being title contenders that year. However, the man in charge was one of Arsenal’s most influential managers, Herbert Chapman, who laid the foundations for the North Londoners’ imminent future success, as well as changing the name of the closest tube station from Gillespie Road to Arsenal, amongst a number of revolutionary changes such as introducing white sleeves on the shirts during the early 1930s. His influence would eventually lead Arsenal to their first major trophy triumph in 1930 . Dixie Dean Faces Arsenal Chasing History On 5 May 1928, the Gunners travelled to Goodison Park to face Everton at their greatest, who had already been crowned league champions for the third time in their history prior to the famous game about to unfold. The official attendance was 48,715, although some accounts estimated that around 60,000 keen spectators were packed inside Goodison Park, waiting for history to be made. The Toffees featured arguably the greatest striker to ever play the game. His name was Dixie Dean, who only ever wanted to play for Everton after having been taken to watch the Merseysiders win the title during the 1914/15 season by his dad, before the football calendar was postponed for a few years due to the outbreak of the First World War. Dean was in search of breaking the English Football League record for the most goals scored in a season, which George Camsell had set with Middlesbrough not long beforehand, with 59 strikes in the Second Division before they were eventually promoted to the First Division in 1927. The only way he could set the bar was if he achieved an elusive hat-trick. The occasion also saw Arsenal legend Charlie Buchan make his final professional appearance before retiring from the game. Dean later suggested that Buchan showed little celebration of one of football’s most historic feats in the English game, perhaps feeling disappointed that Dixie’s record had overshadowed his own farewell. science.description: null You just ordered a Pizza Hut and a two-liter bottle of Mountain Dew. You put on "Space Jam" to watch the greatest of all time team up with the Looney Tunes. It's a perfect evening… in 1996 or 2026. The entire concept of "Space Jam" is so '90s that you swear you can hear Los Del Rio in the background mouthing, "Dale a tu cuerpo alegría, Macarena." As ridiculous as an intergalactic basketball match may sound, it's a perfect example of how even the strangest idea can work if you commit to it fully. In case you thought you hallucinated the whole thing, no, you didn't, as the Looney Tunes find themselves in quite the predicament in this live-action-animation hybrid. A bunch of aliens known as the Nerdlucks arrive on Earth to abduct the Tunes and take them back as attractions to the outer-space amusement park known as Moron Mountain (shockingly nobody has claimed that subreddit, so do your thing, Internet!). Being a wheeling-and-dealing wabbit, though, Bugs Bunny proposes a winner-takes-all basketball game between the Tunes and the tiny Nerdlucks. Unfortunately, the crafty aliens use their tech to steal the talent from ballers like Charles Barkley and Muggsy Bogues and turn themselves into the scary and skilled Monstars. So, Bugs and friends reach out to Michael Jordan, who recently switched from basketball to baseball, to help the Tune Squad win this intergalactic b-ball matchup and their freedom, because if anybody can do it, Air Jordan (Hare Jordan?) can. Oh, Bill Murray also shows up here a few times. Why? Because he can! (Image credit: Warner Bros. Pictures) "Space Jam" is a spin on the classic sci-fi trope of resolving high-stakes conflicts through sports. In 1975, "Death Race 2000" introduced a world where people drive like hooligans and bash into each other to get ahead and win races (ironically, this is the regular experience on any public road now). Meanwhile, in the same year, "Rollerball" demonstrated how to use extreme sports as a plot device whereby brutality trumped any kind of skill in the arena. Yet "Space Jam" took this concept, cartoonified it for a family-friendly audience, and challenged the conflict resolution approaches of other alien invasion movies from 1996. While " Independence Day " saw the heroes trying to destroy the mothership and "Mars Attacks" featured humans running away from "Ack! Ack"-ing extraterrestrials with ray guns, this film used the court to settle the score. It's an innovative way to deal with interplanetary matters, that's for sure. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 15, 1988: The 300-foot Green Bank Telescope collapses suddenly, leaving a huge pile of wreckage in West Virginia
science.description: null On Nov. 15, 1988, a 300-foot radio telescope in Green Bank, West Virginia suddenly collapsed. It happened at 9:46 p.m. on a clear night with no strong winds. When the observatory staff showed up to work the next morning, they were greeted by a huge pile of wreckage. The telescope collapsed under its own weight after a key structural element called a "gusset plate" failed. This was one of four connecting plates that held the telescope's large, metal beams together. Investigators found that these gusset plates were not built to last the 26 years that this telescope had been in use. Three years later, construction began on a new telescope. The Green Bank Telescope was even bigger and more sensitive, and it began science operations in 2001. (Image credit: NRAO/AUI/NSF) Why it mattered When the 300-foot telescope first debuted, it was not just the United States' largest radio observatory, but the largest such facility in the world. But its quick construction — just two years — led to it having to be significantly upgraded later. "In 1970, the 300-foot’s surface had become so warped from maintenance crews, snow, and its own weight that a new finer-meshed aluminum surface was installed," the website for the National Radio Astronomy Observatory reads. "A larger traveling feed was also installed at the prime focus." The collapse, however, was no one's fault. "Unforeseeable stress factors cracked a steel connector plate," wrote the NRAO. The Green Bank Telescope collapse left a mass of twisted debris behind. (Image credit: NRAO/AUI/NSF) During its years of observations, the 300-foot telescope contirbuted to the discovery of dark matter and the realization that pulsars come from supernova explosions. "One of the most important products to come out of the 300-foot telescope was an all-sky survey of radio objects called the Green Bank 6cm Survey. Nearly every northern hemisphere radio object studied by any other telescope is from a catalog compiled using this telescope," reads the NRAO website. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

science.title: Why hasn't the 'Blaze Star' exploded yet? Astronomers weigh in on what to expect
science.description: null For the past two years, stargazers have waited with bated breath for a "new" light to appear in the night sky, born of one of the most cataclysmic events known to occur in the cosmos — a nova explosion. But what is the "Blaze Star" T. Coronae Borealis, and why is it so difficult to predict when its overdue brightening will occur? We turned to the experts to find out. What is T. Coronae Borealis? T. Coronae Borealis — or T CrB for short — isn't a single star, but rather a binary system containing a dense white dwarf star and a bloated red giant. Over a period of around 80 years, the white dwarf's gravity strips material from the red giant until it hits a critical threshold. Next comes a dramatic nova explosion that causes the star to flare to 1,000 times its usual brightness before gradually settling down and repeating the cycle. Why is it so challenging to predict T. CrB's nova flare? "T CrB *will* erupt sometime soon," Bradley Schaefer of the Louisiana State University Department of Physics and Astronomy told Space.com in an email. "Everyone is very confident on this. But we cannot make high-accuracy measures of the rate of gas falling onto the surface of the white dwarf, and we do not have a high accuracy measure of the trigger mass for the big hydrogen bomb." Schaefer continued. Historical observations reveal that the last nova eruption reached Earth in 1946, which places us well inside the window for another dramatic brightening of T. CrBb. However, the unpredictability of the white dwarf's feeding makes it difficult to pin down exactly when the explosion will become visible from Earth. An animation of T. CrB brightening. (Image credit: NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center Conceptual Image Lab) "The exact date of the upcoming T CrB eruption depends primarily on how fast the gas coming from its companion star is accumulating on the surface of the white dwarf," explained Schaefer. "When some specific trigger mass has accumulated, then T CrB will erupt. For the last 80 years, we have been watching the gas pile up on the white dwarf surface, and we know that it must be near the trigger threshold." Astronomers have tried to predict T CrB's brightening by comparing a recent fluctuation in the light of the distant star system to a similar event that occurred in the runup to the 1946 event. "There have already been some dimming and brightening episodes that caused excitement but did not yet turn into the main event," Elizabeth Hays, lab chief at NASA's Astroparticle Physics Laboratory at the Goddard Spaceflight Center , told Space.com in an email. "It is likely that the nova will happen in the next few years but we still don't know exactly when. I can't give you a guaranteed prediction, but I will be a little surprised if it gets to 2030, or 84 years past the last eruption." science.title: How escaping gases ripped apart a comet and caused it to become thousands of times brighter
science.description: A comet dazzled this summer as the sun’s heat caused ice beneath its surface to turn to gas and rip out through its surface, spewing hundreds of billions of pounds' worth of dust into space and causing the comet to brighten by thousands of times. Comet 220P/McNaught was discovered by the prolific Australian comet discoverer Robert McNaught in 2004. It is a periodic comet, the 220th discovered, meaning that it comes back again and again on a regular basis – in 220P’s case, once every five-and-a-half years when it gets about as close to the sun as Mars . Other than that, 220P is fairly nondescript, usually languishing at a feeble brightness fainter than magnitude +15, out of reach of most amateur telescopes. There has been little else to say about the comet, until this year. On June 14, as it headed towards perihelion – the closest point in its orbit to the sun, at a distance from our star of 1.5 times the distance between the Earth and the sun (known as an astronomical unit) , 220P suddenly and without warning burst into life. On 31 May, the comet was languishing at magnitude +17.39 (the higher the magnitude, the fainter an object is), but within less than 14 hours it had dramatically brightened to magnitude +11.05, bringing it into range for observation with small amateur telescopes. By June 2, 220P was up to magnitude +8.23 and was technically visible for a short while in 10x50 binoculars from a dark site, prompting amateur astronomers and astrophotographers to chase down this rare event. By perihelion, the comet had faded back to magnitude +12, but more was to come. A second outburst began at the end of July, brightening from magnitude +14 on 28 July to magnitude 6.1 by 6 August. Telling the tale of a dirty snowball Comets are often referred to as dirty snowballs, and beneath their dusty crust are ices made from various volatiles, including water, carbon dioxide and nitrogen. Solar heating, even at the distance of Mars, can cause these ices to rapidly sublimate into gases, and the pressure of the escaping gas rips the surface apart, spewing huge amounts of dust in to space. Models based on observations of 220P’s outburst indicate that it spewed out between tens of billions and hundreds of billions of pounds’ worth of cometary dust that filled the comet’s coma, the diffuse 'atmosphere' that clings to the comet’s solid nucleus. The dust particles, which are just millionths of a meter across, expanded outwards from the comet at about 1,280 feet (390 meters) per second, scattering sunlight and causing the coma to substantially brighten. "We have concluded that the comet detached localized parts of its crust, creating a dust-rich envelope that increased [the comet’s brightness by] 250 times in half a day," Josep M. Trigo-Rodríguez, of the Institut de Ciències de l’Espai and the Institute of Space Studies of Catalonia in Spain, said in a statement . science.title: What's next for SpaceX's Starship after epic Flight 15 chopsticks catch?
science.description: null Starship may have just made history, but it still has some work to do to get fully up and running. The megarocket launched on its 15th test flight on Friday (Nov. 13), aiming to pull off a dramatic and unprecedented twofer. SpaceX wanted to bring both Starship elements — its Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage — back to the launch pad at its Starbase site in Texas to be caught by the tower's "chopstick" arms. It didn't happen with Super Heavy; the booster diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown on Friday evening after experiencing a low-fuel alarm. But Ship came home successfully , nestling into the tower's arms in a soft and unprecedented embrace on Saturday afternoon (Nov. 14), 22.5 hours after lifting off. Long-distance view of Ship's historic landing on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) SpaceX has caught Super Heavy on three test flights to date. But it had never caught a Ship before; indeed, it had never even tried before Saturday. It's tougher and riskier to catch Ship; the upper stage flies much higher and faster than Super Heavy, so its return trip is much more more involved. Saturday was therefore a very big day for the company. "That was the holy grail of spaceflight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel," SpaceX spokesperson Dan Huot said during the company's landing webcast on Saturday. "We caught a Starship, and now everything changes." The F light 15 mission plan gave us a sneak peek at the future: The double catch will be standard on operational Starship missions, as this recovery strategy will enable rapid inspection, refurbishment and reflight of the megarocket, according to SpaceX. And the company is indeed planning on rapid reflight. Elon Musk has said that SpaceX is targeting 10,000 Starship launches per year by 2030, which works out to more than one liftoff every hour on average. Why such a mind-boggling cadence? Because SpaceX plans to build megaconstellations far larger than anything circling Earth today. For example, it wants its next-gen Starlink V3 broadband network to consist of 100,000 satellites . And its planned Starmind AI data-center constellation will be 10 times bigger than that, featuring one million spacecraft , if all goes to plan. For perspective: SpaceX's current-gen Starlink network in low Earth orbit (LEO), by far the largest constellation ever assembled, is about 11,000 strong at the moment. A look at the 33 Raptor engines of Starship's Super Heavy booster during the vehicle's Flight 15 test launch on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: Josh Dinner, Space.com/Future) Rocket recovery is only part of the reuse equation, of course; there's also refurbishment and reflight. And that gets us back to the "work left to do" discussion, for SpaceX has yet to demonstrate rapid reflight with either Super Heavy or Ship. science.title: 'Alien: Fireteam Elite 2' is a good old-fashioned bug hunt, ironically plagued by bugs
science.description: The first Aliens: Fireteam Elite was among my favorite Alien video games , and there were a lot of reasons to be excited for a sequel. At Summer Game Fest 2026 , we learned of many smart changes and improvements to the formula, and I was eager to go bug-hunting again. A new campaign, fully reworked classes, and four-player co-op. What could go wrong? Months later, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2's debut has been difficult, mostly due to glaring tech issues. Despite this, it's still a welcome jolt of action for a franchise that's been focusing on making the Xenomorphs scary again in recent years. Alien: Romulus (2024) and Alien: Earth (2025) have reestablished the acid-blooded Xenomorphs as bona fide horror icons, while games like Aliens: Dark Descent bet on tense real-time tactics and squad management; Rogue Incursion spooked VR and non-VR players alike; and we even have Isolation 2 's pure survival horror to look forward to. Rough edges aside, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 is a necessary return to mindless shooting and treating the Xenos as a relentless horde, dropping the stalking and slasher-inspired murders in favor of sci-fi shootouts and macho one-liners. It's far from a novel idea — even the original game is only five years old — but a classic for a reason. Another glorious day in the Corps (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) Believe it or not, another colony has fallen prey to the Xenomorphs in Fireteam Elite 2. The familiar setup takes a new team of Colonial Marines to a mining facility on LV-558, where contact has been lost with the first wave of Marines that went in to deal with the threat. This isn't first contact; the Marines are more than used to bug hunts by now, which means there's less exposition to cut through before getting to the Xeno-blasting chaos. The writing certainly won't stun the Academy (and there's definitely too much of it in between missions), but the agility here is appreciated. We've fought these aliens many, many times before. Fireteam Elite 2 is smart enough to sidestep fake tension and just hit the ground running. (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) All the design changes and upgrades reinforce the intent to make the ultimate Aliens action game. Classes have more defined roles and access to better, more destructive sci-fi weapons, and the upgrade to four-player fireteams is welcome when aliens and hostile synths won't stop pouring in. Tired of replaying campaign missions on higher difficulties and with modifiers? Prepare for the worst in this shooter's version of the classic horde mode. At its best, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 understands why James Cameron's masterpiece still holds up. During the biggest Xenomorph onslaughts — when the bullets are flying and acid is spraying — the game's shortcomings and jankier elements fade away. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 14, 1969: NASA's Apollo 12 astronauts launch to the moon on a 'pinpoint landing' lunar mission
science.description: null On Nov. 14, 1969, the Apollo 12 mission launched to the moon. This was the second moon landing of the Apollo program. The two astronauts on board were Pete Conrad , commander, and Alan Bean , the lunar module pilot. Astronaut Richard Gordon , the command module pilot, stayed in the command module and orbited the moon while his crewmates went to the surface. The astronauts made a pinpoint landing in a lunar mare called the Ocean of Storms. The previous moon mission, Apollo 11 , drifted far from the planned landing zone. But Apollo 12 landed close to a scientific target. That target was a robotic lander called Surveyor 3 . Scientists wanted to look at Surveyor 3 to see how well the spacecraft lasted on the moon since it landed there more than two years earlier. The Apollo 12 moonwalkers also performed a lot of moon science. The astronauts picked up 75 pounds of moon rocks. Most of the rocks were basalts that formed from molten lava. These basalts showed the Apollo 12 landing site is more than 3 billion years old. The Apollo 12 astronauts on NASA's second crewed moon landing mission. They are (left to right) are Charles Conrad Jr., Richard F. Gordon Jr., and Alan L. Bean. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered Apollo 12 proved that the Apollo 11 moon landing was not just a one-off stunt while setting the stage for even more ambitious missions. To truly explore the moon and advance our understanding of how our solar system formed, the follow-on Apollo flights needed to be able to land where the geologists had identified as areas of interest. Apollo 12, with its touchdown in proximity to the Surveyor probe, proved this was possible. The Apollo 12 astronauts visited NASA's Surveyor 3 lander and took samples of it back to Earth. (Image credit: NASA) The launch of Apollo 12 also underscored the importance of having a well-prepared Mission Control team, an asset that would be critical to outcome of the next mission, Apollo 13. The ability to recover from a complete electrical short out with the simple call of a through of a switch "SCE to AUX" proved that knowing every detail about how the spacecraft worked was key to a successful program. science.title: 'Now everything changes': SpaceX catches Starship upper stage for 1st time ever (video)
science.description: null SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever today (Nov. 14), a landmark achievement that could unlock the giant vehicle's immense potential. Starship launched on its 15th test flight on Friday evening (Nov. 13), rising into the sky from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas. The mission plan called for bringing both of the vehicle's stages back to Starbase and catching them with the launch tower's "chopstick" arms — an unprecedented total recovery of an orbital rocket . That didn't happen; Starship's Super Heavy booster diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown on Friday after experiencing a low-fuel alarm. But Ship succeeded in its attempt, notching a huge milestone for SpaceX and its dream of full rocket reuse. "That was the missing link," SpaceX's Dan Huot said during the company's landing webcast today, his voice thick with emotion. "That was the holy grail of spaceflight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel. We caught a Starship, and now everything changes." SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever today (Nov. 14), a landmark achievement that could unlock the giant vehicle's immense potential. (Image credit: Josh Dinner/Space.com) The Ship catch occurred today at 4:20 p.m. EST (2120 GMT; 3:20 p.m. local Texas time), roughly 22.5 hours after Flight 15 lifted off. Many SpaceX employees went outside to watch the vehicle, known as Ship 42, descend through the clouds toward its Starbase launch tower, which the company calls "Mechazilla." And they got quite a show: Ship 42 nestled gently into Mechazilla's waiting arms, while "Baby Come Back" played over SpaceX's landing webcast. "This is so incredible to see," SpaceX's Jessie Anderson said during the livestream. "One of the most incredible and historic engineering feats of all time has just happened right in front of our eyes." Why was this such a big deal? SpaceX had already caught Super Heavy — on three previous Starship test flights, in fact. But it had never tried before with Ship. The upper stage is a tougher target, for it flies higher, farther and faster than the booster. Indeed, on Flight 15, Ship 42 came all the way back down from orbit. Ship 42 comes in for its landing on Nov. 14, 2026. science.title: See Jupiter and Mars make a spectacular close approach overnight Nov. 15-16
science.description: null Heads up stargazers! Mars meets Jupiter for a spectacular rendezvous in the heart of the constellation Leo on the night of Nov. 15-16, and they won't be this close again until July 2029. Jupiter and Mars will appear a little over 1 degree from each other as they rise over the eastern horizon around midnight for viewers in the U.S., as the blue-white light of the main-sequence star Regulus glows below, according to In-The-Sky . It's all a trick of perspective, but spectacular nonetheless. In reality Mars and Jupiter are separated by a gulf of over 368 million miles (592 million kilometers), while the light from Regulus has travelled for some 79 light-years before reaching Earth . The spectacular display occurs just once every 2-2.5 years , when Mars catches up to Jupiter as it plies its more distant orbit, making the pair appear side by side from our Earthly vantage point — an event known to astronomers as an appulse. Jupiter, Mars and Regulus will appear close together on the night of Nov. 15-16. (Image credit: Created by Anthony Wood in Canva.) Both Mars and Jupiter are "superior planets" whose orbits exist beyond that of Earth. As a result their disks always appear full to us through the eyepiece of a telescope, unlike the inner planets Mercury and Venus , which exhibit moon-like phases as they circle the sun . A 6-inch telescope can reveal the wildly differing natures of the solar system worlds. Slew your scope to Jupiter to spot the gargantuan cloud bands (and zones) that ring the gas giant , formed from masses of ammonia and water that travel in different directions through Jupiter's hydrogen and helium atmosphere, driven by powerful jet streams. How to measure distances in the night sky using your outstretched hand. (Image credit: Created in Canva Pro) Mars, meanwhile, appears as a reddish, ochre disk complete with dark surface features, where basaltic rock has been scoured clean of the iron-rich dust that covers much of its surface, according to NASA . Interested in seeing and capturing the planets for yourself?
